s_setup.text: First-run wizard as one stage, not a form: a five-step pipeline, a radar that sweeps the network for the router, the found router as a glass card, sign-in method as segmented buttons with an app key (default) or the router password, the host key as a fingerprint grid to approve, firmware detection and the look step. Try: the step buttons (Back and Next move the pipeline), App key or Password, the reveal eye, Approve host key, Tweaks > stage success (burst and tick) and failure (shake and reason), firmware, lang. Stands for: the app first-run screens: owner account, connect, host key approval. Unbuilt in the app: Network scan radar, firmware detection summary and the look step are design only.

s_startup.text: The two cards a person can see between signing in and the app being ready. The loading card: "Opening your router", a spinner, a progress bar and the count "Loading features: 120 of 182", so a slow start is visibly still moving. The start-up error card: "The app could not start", the error text in a monospace box so it can be copied into a report, and two ways out, "Clear saved settings and retry" and "Try again". Try: the two state buttons (Loading, Could not start); the slider under the loading card (the bar and the count follow); Try again and Clear saved settings and retry (both go back to loading from zero; the second one says what was cleared); Tweaks > motion calm (the spinner stops and the count still tells you where it is), lang, dark, accent. Stands for: the loading card and the start-up error card the app shows after sign-in. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the app. The slider is for the canvas only.

s_routers.text: Saved routers at phone width. At the top, the badge that sits on the top bar of the whole app for as long as a Testing router is in use ("Testing router: Bench"), so a change meant for the bench is never made at home by mistake. "The router in use" card with a name field, a Main or Testing choice and Save. The list of saved routers with Main and Testing chips, "In use" on the current one, "Use this router" on the others, and remove. The second section is the key choice on the connect screen: Create a key, Make a new key (asks first) and Use a key I already have, with the refusal for a key that is protected by a passphrase. Try: Use this router on Home (the Testing badge leaves); switch the router in use between Main and Testing and Save (the chip and the badge follow); type a new name and Save; remove a router that is not in use; the Connection keys section: each of the three choices, Make a new key then Cancel or confirm, and the two sample key files (the one with a passphrase is refused with the reason); Tweaks > role viewer, lang, dark, stage. Stands for: the saved routers screen, the Testing badge on the top bar and the key choices on the connect screen. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the app. The two sample key files stand in for the file chooser.

s_main.text: The dashboard as a bento: a hero with the live download rate counting up over an aurora, a glass live-traffic chart that draws in, four tonal number tiles with sparklines, the home network map with packets moving along every link, band gauges, quick switches that queue into pending changes, busiest devices, an hourly heat map and recent changes with undo. Try: the quick switches (the dock rises with a count and Apply under guard), the chart range buttons, Tweaks > stage loading (skeleton shimmer) and empty, motion calm (everything stills on the designed frame), accent, dark, lang, role viewer. Stands for: the app overview screen: model, firmware, uptime, clients. Unbuilt in the app: Live traffic chart source, network map, heat map and quick switches are design only.

s_notifications.text: Notification centre: a hero with the unread count and a week of activity as bars, a live stack of toasts sliding in, the feed as rows with kind avatars, status chips and inline actions, per-kind switches, quiet hours as a paintable day strip and a slider for how long toasts stay. Try: the kind filter chips, the per-kind switches, quiet hours cells (click one, then another), the toast seconds slider, Tweaks > stage empty and failure. Stands for: the simple toasts the app shows after an action. Unbuilt in the app: The centre, snooze, per-kind switches and quiet hours are design only.

s_modes.text: Seven large mode cards (Gaming, Bedtime, Guest party, Work from home, Privacy DNS, Lock it down, Away). Each one is a real bundle of router changes. Tapping a card opens a preview sheet listing every change with its old and new value; Apply runs the bundle through preview, guard and undo; an active card shows On now and a one-tap Undo. Try: tap any card (the sheet rises from the right with the exact changes), Apply under guard, then Undo on the card; open Guest party to see the QR card; Tweaks > role viewer (cards open, apply is off), stage success and failure, lang. Stands for: the write path that already exists (preview, connection-loss guard, change history with undo), applied to several settings at once. Unbuilt in the app: Modes do not exist in the app; the bundles, the access limit timer and the QR card are design only.

s_modebuilder.text: A builder canvas for your own mode: a palette of real router settings grouped by area on the left, a dotted canvas on the right that holds the settings in the mode as cards, each with a real switch for the value the mode will set and a remove button, plus the mode name (with a counter), icon, colour and when it turns itself off. Try: click a palette card (it lifts and the canvas shows a dashed drop outline), then click the canvas to drop it; flip the switch on a card; remove a card; the icon and colour buttons; Tweaks > stage failure for the conflict message. Stands for: the settings catalogue (each palette card is one catalogue entry). Unbuilt in the app: The builder does not exist in the app. On the canvas a drag is two clicks (pick, then drop); the app would use pointer drag with the same keyboard route.

s_devices.text: Everyone on the network as cards in a bento, not a table: a hero with the device count and a band split, each device with an icon tile, signal bars, live rate sparkline, status chip and inline switches for block and reserve; a focused device panel with priority, owner and address pickers. Try: the filter chips, block and reserve switches on any row (the dock counts them), the focused device picker, priority buttons and the last-octet address stepper, Tweaks > role viewer, stage empty and failure. Stands for: the app devices screen (name, address, MAC, band). Unbuilt in the app: Signal history, per-device live rate, owner assignment and bulk actions are design only.

s_lockip.text: Lock IP on the device list at phone width. Each row has a one-tap Lock IP or Unlock IP button, the words "IP locked" as a tag beside the address (not a colour alone), an icon button to lock the device to a different address, and a Kick shortcut. Ticking rows brings up the selection bar with Lock IPs and Unlock IPs. Docked at the bottom of the list is the waiting change, written out ("Lock IP 198.51.100.103 → kitchen-speaker"), with Review. Review opens the Changes waiting section: the changes panel and the four-key confirmation. Key 4 offers "No keyboard? Tap in order:" with the buttons 3, 1, 2, which is the touch form of the key combination. Try: Lock IP on Living-TV (the docked line counts a second change); Unlock IP on Pat-Laptop; the pencil on a row (an address stepper opens; Lock to this address queues it); tick and untick rows, then Lock IPs or Unlock IPs in the selection bar; Review, or the Changes waiting section button; in the panel turn key 1, type kitchen-speaker for key 2, tap Press and hold for key 3, then tap 1, 2, 3 in order for key 4 (the buttons are laid out 3, 1, 2, and a wrong tap starts again); Turn all four keys; Discard; Tweaks > role viewer, stage success and failure, lang, dark. Stands for: the device list with Lock IP, the pending changes panel and the four-key confirmation, as the app shows them on a phone. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the app. In the app key 3 is a real press and hold; on this board one tap stands in for it.

s_kickban.text: The Kick and ban screen at phone width. A card for the person who was paused, with the link to the Unkick page. A Paused now list where each row says how the device is held, until when ("until 19:49, 30 min left"), who did it and the note, with an Unkick or Unban button. The device list, each row with its owner ("belongs to Your brother") and a Kick button. The Kick sheet: the impact line, the three ways to pause with an explanation under each, a dashed box that points to the speed limiter instead, the duration choices from 15 minutes to "Until lifted (ban)", a note for the person, and one action that reads Kick, Ban or Disconnect. A Recent log. Try: the three section buttons (Paused now, Devices, Recent); Unkick on Living-TV and Unban on Alex-Tablet (the row leaves and the log gains a line); Kick on Game-Console (the impact line turns into the brother warning and shakes once); in the sheet pick each way to pause (Disconnect hides the duration and renames the action), pick "Until lifted (ban)" (the action becomes Ban and the ban note appears), then Kick (the device moves to Paused now); Copy the link; Tweaks > role viewer (nothing can be kicked), motion standard (the warning stops shaking), lang, dark, stage. Stands for: the Kick and ban screen in the app, including the sheet opened from the device list. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the app. The brother wording follows the household setting, which this board fixes to one name.

s_unkick.text: The public Unkick page, which needs no sign-in: the page a paused person opens on their own device. A breathing circle, "Your internet is paused", why and the note that was left, "until 19:49 (30 min left), by Pat", and one big "Unkick me" button (it reads "Unban me" for a ban). Under it, the line that says the page can only lift a pause on the device you are using now and never shows anyone else's devices. The other states are here too: not paused, the router does not know this device, and lifted ("Unkicked. You are back online."). Try: the five state buttons (Paused, Banned, Not paused, Unknown, Lifted); Unkick me (the circle turns into a green tick and the title changes); Check again; Tweaks > lang (the page follows the language of the browser), dark, accent, motion standard and calm (the circle stops breathing). Stands for: the Unkick page the app serves without sign-in, opened from the link on the Kick and ban screen. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the app. The state buttons at the top are for the canvas only.

t_kick.text: Kick, ban and the public Unkick page

s_wifi.text: Three band tiles in strong tonal colours, each with a radio switch, a channel gauge, width as segmented buttons, power as a slider and the client count; a radar that sweeps for neighbouring networks; the network name with a counter; security as segmented buttons; the password with strength; and the guest network with its QR card. Try: flip a radio, change width or power (the dock rises), security buttons, the reveal eye, guest switch, Tweaks > stage success and failure (both are guard outcomes), firmware, role viewer. Stands for: the Wi-Fi band settings in the catalogue: radio, name, hidden, security, password, channel, width, power, guest. Unbuilt in the app: The neighbour radar and the guest QR card are design only; the channel spectrum editor is its own board.

s_mesh.text: The mesh as a live map: router and two nodes with backhaul links, packets flowing along healthy links and a dashed amber link for the weak one; a tile per node with a backhaul quality gauge, uplink type as segmented buttons and its clients; roaming assistant threshold as a slider. Try: the uplink buttons and switches on a node tile, the roaming slider, Restart node, Tweaks > stage empty and failure, firmware, role viewer. Stands for: the AiMesh domain in the catalogue (node list is read from the router). Unbuilt in the app: Topology map, backhaul quality, per-node clients and node actions are design only.

s_network.text: The internet side: a hero with the public address and a live latency line, connection type as large segmented buttons, DNS as resolver cards with a privacy switch, a world path from router to provider to the internet with moving packets, dynamic DNS and the WAN details as real controls. Try: the connection type buttons, the DNS privacy switch and resolver picker, MTU slider, dynamic DNS switch (the dock counts the changes and Apply runs under the guard), Tweaks > stage success and failure. Stands for: the internet domain in the catalogue: connection type, DNS servers, DNS privacy, MTU, dynamic DNS. Unbuilt in the app: Latency history, the path picture and resolver speed comparison are design only.

s_lan.text: The local network without a single typed address: the router address as a four-part picker with a stepper, the prefix as a stepper beside a network-and-host bar, the DHCP pool as a miniature address map, reservations as device rows with address steppers, and port forwards as rows with port chips and switches. Try: the last-octet stepper and prefix stepper (the bar moves), lease slider, reservation switches, port presets, forward switches, Tweaks > stage success and failure (changing the router address runs under the guard). Stands for: the local network and port forwarding domains: router address, mask, DHCP start and end, lease time, reservations, forwards. Unbuilt in the app: The pickers and mini map are design; the app has a plain IPv4 field. The full editors are the Address map and Rule canvas boards.

s_qos.text: Who is using the line right now as a stacked live picture: a hero with total throughput, a stream per kind of traffic, a gauge for how full the line is, the mode as segmented buttons, the line speeds as sliders, and the busiest devices with a priority control on every row. Try: the mode buttons, line sliders, the High/Normal/Low buttons on each device, the game boost switch, then Apply in the dock; Open the priority board for the ordered editor. Stands for: traffic priority (QoS) in the catalogue: mode, upload and download bandwidth. Unbuilt in the app: Live per-kind streams and waiting-time measurements are design only.

t_network.text: Internet, local network, ports, traffic priority

s_security.text: One security picture: a score ring in the hero, the three open findings as large cards with a one-switch fix each, blocked knocks on a world-hours heat map, and summaries of firewall, parental controls and VPN that link to their own boards. Try: flip the fix switches on the finding cards (each joins the dock), Fix all three, Tweaks > stage success and failure, firmware, role viewer. Stands for: firewall, WPS, remote access and VPN server switches in the catalogue, read together. Unbuilt in the app: The score, findings and blocked-knock heat map are design only.

s_firewall.text: The firewall as a shield, not a settings list: a hero with knocks blocked today and a live strike chart, big switch tiles for the four protections, the open doors as port chips with switches, and a blocked-address list with a block-range picker. Try: the protection switches, the door switches, the block length buttons and prefix stepper, Tweaks > stage empty (firewall off) and failure. Stands for: the firewall domain: firewall on/off, DoS protection, respond to ping, logged packets. Unbuilt in the app: Live blocked chart, the address block list with ranges and the outside port test are design only. The lane editor is the Rule canvas board.

s_parental.text: Family time as people, not rules: a hero with today's remaining time as a big number and ring, one tonal card per person with their devices, a pause switch and a daily limit slider, the week painted on a grid, and content filters as chips. Try: Pause on a person card, the daily limit slider, paint the week (click one cell then another), the filter chips, Add 30 minutes, Tweaks > stage failure, role viewer. Stands for: parental controls in the catalogue: time scheduling per device (MULTIFILTER keys). Unbuilt in the app: People grouping, daily limits, bonus time and content filter chips are design only; the full paint editor is the Paint schedules board.

s_vpn.text: VPN both ways: a hero with connected peers and a tunnel throughput line inside a rotating ring, the WireGuard and OpenVPN servers as tiles with switches and port pickers, peers as rows with a QR card, and client tunnels with health gauges. Try: server switches, the port presets and stepper, peer switches, the kill switch; on stock firmware WireGuard shows the reason it is unavailable on this model instead of disappearing. Stands for: the VPN domain: OpenVPN and WireGuard server switches and ports. Unbuilt in the app: Peer management with QR, client tunnel health and throughput are design only. Per-device routing is the VPN Director board.

s_mapeditor.text: A drag-and-drop map of the real network: the router and two AiMesh nodes with backhaul quality on the links, every device as a round tile hanging from the node it uses, packets moving along live links, and a side panel for the picked device (rename, reserve, block, bind to a node). Try: click a device (it lifts), then click another node: the device glides across, its link redraws and a pending change appears; flip Block (its link goes dashed and packets stop) and Reserve; Tweaks > role viewer, stage, motion calm. Stands for: the devices list, DHCP reservations, MAC filter and the AiMesh node list, shown as one picture. Unbuilt in the app: The map editor is design only. Drag is pick-then-place on the canvas.

s_rulecanvas.text: A rule canvas with a lane per destination (the router itself and each device). Every rule is a card with its port as a chip, a protocol tag and a real on/off switch. Two rules that claim the same outside port are outlined in red, shake once and are counted in the hero. Try: two rules clash on TCP 443 when the board opens: switch one off and the red outline and the count clear; click a card to pick it, then click another lane to move the rule to that device; build a new rule with the port picker, protocol and device picker, then Add rule; remove a card. Stands for: the port forwarding list and firewall switches in the catalogue. Unbuilt in the app: The lane canvas, conflict detection and outside port test are design only.

s_schedulepaint.text: Two week grids you paint instead of filling in: internet hours for a child's device and the hours the Wi-Fi radios stay on. Each has a paint or erase brush, presets, a live count of painted hours and a device or band picker. Try: click one cell, then another: the whole block between them is painted; switch the brush to Erase and do it again; the presets (School nights, Weekends, Always); pick another device; the dock shows the pending change. Stands for: the parental time schedule and the wireless schedule in the catalogue. Unbuilt in the app: The paint grids are design only; the app shows these as plain values. Drag-painting becomes click-then-click on the canvas.

s_priorityboard.text: A drag-to-order board: seven kinds of traffic as ranked cards, each showing the share of the line it is guaranteed, with up and down buttons; below it, four priority lanes that hold the devices; and line speed limits as sliders. Try: the up and down arrows on a card (cards trade places, shares re-flow); click a card grip then another card to move it there; click a device, then a lane, to change its level; the upload and download sliders. Stands for: traffic priority (QoS) settings in the catalogue: mode, order, bandwidth. Unbuilt in the app: The ordered board and per-device lanes are design only; the app shows these as selects.

s_spectrum.text: The air around the house as a spectrum: every neighbouring network is a grey bell curve at its channel, yours is a bright curve you move by picking a channel and a width. A live score says how crowded your position is and one button jumps to the quietest channel. Try: click the channel buttons: your curve slides and the score recomputes; change the width (the curve widens and swallows more neighbours); switch band; Move to the quietest channel; Tweaks > stage failure for the radar message. Stands for: channel and channel width for each band in the catalogue. Unbuilt in the app: The neighbour scan and the spectrum view are design only. Dragging the curve becomes picking a channel on the canvas.

s_portcanvas.text: The back of the router drawn as a panel of real jacks. Each port glows in the colour of the network it carries. Pick a network card, then click a port to carry it there. A row per port has a real switch for tagged or untagged, and a provider profile fills the panel in one go. Try: pick the IPTV card, click LAN 3 (its jack changes colour and the pending dock rises); flip Tagged on a port row; the provider profile buttons; Tweaks > stage failure (the guard refuses to cut this computer off). Stands for: the IPTV, LAN port and VLAN settings (switch_wantag, switch_stb_x and related keys). Unbuilt in the app: The back-panel canvas and profile presets are design only.

s_vpndirector.text: Devices on the left, three ways out on the right (the plain internet and two VPN tunnels). A coloured stream with moving packets runs from every device to the way out it uses. Pick a device, then click a destination: its stream bends over to the new one. Try: click a device card, then a destination: the stream re-routes and recolours; the kill switch and tunnel switches; Tweaks > firmware stock (the whole canvas shows locked with the reason, because VPN Director is Merlin only), stage failure. Stands for: VPN Director policy rules on Asuswrt-Merlin (vpndirector_rulelist) and the VPN client switches. Unbuilt in the app: The routing canvas and leak test are design only.

s_dhcpmap.text: The whole 198.51.100.0/24 subnet as a grid of 256 cells, coloured by what each address is: the router, reserved, leased now, free inside the pool, free outside it. The pool is the tinted band; its two ends are the ringed cells. Try: click any cell: the nearer end of the pool jumps there, the band, the free count and the fill gauge follow; the start and end steppers; the three presets; shrink the pool until a reservation falls outside and the warning chip appears. Stands for: DHCP start, DHCP end, lease time and the reservation list (dhcp_start, dhcp_end, dhcp_staticlist). Unbuilt in the app: The address map is design only. Dragging a pool edge becomes clicking a cell.

s_storage.text: Storage as a picture of the drive: a hero ring with how full it is, the kinds of files as a stacked bar and tiles, sharing services as switch tiles, people with access as rows with read or write buttons, and drive health with a temperature line. Try: Eject (success) and try again with Tweaks > stage failure (busy), the sharing switches, the per-person access buttons, the sleep slider, Tweaks > stage empty. Stands for: the USB domain: file sharing (Samba), FTP, media server switches. Unbuilt in the app: Usage breakdown by kind, per-person access, health and eject are design only.

s_tools.text: The router's own tools as an instrument panel: a target picker with presets, a ping panel with a live latency line and a big average, a hop-by-hop trace drawn as a path with packets, and the live log as a terminal with level chips and a regex-builder button. Try: the tool buttons, target device picker, count stepper, the level chips on the log, Tweaks > stage success and failure, role viewer (tools still run, they do not change the router). Stands for: the app tools screen (ping, traceroute and name lookup run on the router) and the logs screen. Unbuilt in the app: Live latency line, the drawn trace path and live log streaming are design only.

s_speedlab.text: A speed test that feels like an instrument: a huge dial with a counting number in the hero, phases as a pipeline (latency, download, upload), the run drawn live, history as bars against the plan you pay for, and a schedule with a painted strip for when tests may run. Try: Start (success), the server picker, the plan slider (the "of plan" figure is against it), the schedule cells, Tweaks > stage loading, success and failure. Stands for: nothing yet in the app; the router has a built-in speed test command this would call. Unbuilt in the app: The whole board is design only.

s_utilities.text: Everyday router jobs as big tappable tiles rather than a menu: restart Wi-Fi, wake a sleeping device, share the Wi-Fi as a QR card, find a device by blinking the router lights, night mode for the lights on a painted strip, and a password generator with strength. Try: the device picker and Wake, the QR band buttons, lights switch and brightness slider, night-mode cells, password length slider and character chips, Tweaks > stage success and failure. Stands for: wake-on-LAN and the LED switch exist as router commands and catalogue entries; the rest are composed from existing settings. Unbuilt in the app: QR sharing, the generator and night mode strip are design only.

s_jobs.text: Scheduled jobs on a 24-hour ring and a week grid instead of a table of timer expressions: a hero with the next job counting down, each job as a row with a real switch and a run-now button, the week as a painted grid, and the last runs as a bar strip. Try: job switches, Run now, paint the weekly restart window, the hour stepper, Tweaks > firmware stock (custom scripts lock with the reason), stage failure for a collision. Stands for: the read-only scheduled jobs table the app shows from the router. Unbuilt in the app: Creating and editing jobs, the ring and run history are design only.

t_tools.text: Logs, network tools, router tools, scheduled jobs

s_firmware.text: A firmware update you can watch: a hero with the installed and the offered build, the update as a six-step pipeline with a progress bar and a countdown ring, what changes as chips, the safety net (automatic backup, checksum, what happens if power fails) and build history as a timeline. Try: Update now (success burst) and Tweaks > stage failure (checksum refusal), the update channel buttons, the automatic backup switch, firmware stock (the offered build and channel names change). Stands for: the firmware domain: installed version and the check-for-update command. Unbuilt in the app: In-app flashing, checksum verification, the pipeline and release notes are design only.

s_system.text: The router as a machine: a hero with uptime and three live gauges (processor, memory, temperature), a 24-hour load chart, the clock and time zone as pickers, how the router can be reached (SSH, web page, from outside) as switch tiles with port pickers, and maintenance actions that open the takeover. Try: the access switches (turning SSH off is refused: Tweaks > stage failure), port presets, time zone buttons, the restart action (goes to the takeover board), role operator and viewer. Stands for: the system and maintenance domains: time zone, NTP server, SSH, web access, restart and factory reset actions. Unbuilt in the app: Live gauges and load history are design only.

s_backup.text: Backups as a timeline of snapshots: a hero with how fresh the newest one is, each backup as a card with size, setting count and a restore button, a compare view listing exactly which settings differ from now, the nightly schedule, where copies go and the password that encrypts them. Try: Back up now (success), Restore on an older snapshot (opens the diff), the destination switches, the keep-count slider, Tweaks > stage failure (wrong model refused), role operator (restore is owner only). Stands for: the backup domain: save and restore the router settings file. Unbuilt in the app: Encrypted archive, snapshots timeline, compare view and off-router destinations are design only.

s_advanced.text: Every remaining router value without looking like a spreadsheet: a hero with how many values exist and how many you changed, areas as a heat map of where the changes are, values as rows with the readable label first and the raw key second, each with the right control for its type, and Merlin extras as lockable tiles. Try: the area chips, the controls on each row (switch, stepper, segmented), Show secrets (owner only), Tweaks > firmware stock (Merlin extras lock with the reason), role operator and viewer, stage failure. Stands for: the app advanced table (every nvram value, catalogue label first, secrets masked). Unbuilt in the app: Typed controls per row, the change heat map and Merlin add-on management are design only.

t_router.text: Firmware, system, maintenance, backup, advanced, Merlin

s_changes.text: The write path in one place: a hero with the pending count, each pending change as a before-and-after card with its risk level, the four-step write pipeline (preview, write, guard, keep), history as a timeline with undo on every entry, and who changed what as bars. Try: Apply under guard (success burst), Discard, Undo on a history row, the risk filter chips, Tweaks > stage failure (guard rollback), role viewer (can read, cannot apply). Stands for: the app change history with undo and the write path (preview, connection-loss guard for network changes, two-key confirmation for destructive ones). Unbuilt in the app: Batching several pending changes into one guarded apply and the activity bars are design only.

s_takeover.text: The moment a risky change is live: a full-width guard with a real countdown inside a rotating wavy ring, one large "I am still connected" action, what will be restored if time runs out, the live reconnect signal, and below it the two-key confirmation used for destructive actions (factory reset, firmware), where both keys must be turned. Try: I am still connected (success burst), Roll back now, Tweaks > stage failure (time ran out), the two key switches (the destructive button only arms when both are on), role operator (the second key is owner only). Stands for: the connection-loss guard for network changes and the two-key super confirmation for destructive actions; both exist in the app. Unbuilt in the app: The reconnect signal line and the wavy ring are design; the logic exists.

s_records.text: Exports as something you assemble: pick what goes in (toggle chips), the format (large segmented tiles), the date range on a painted month strip, see a live page preview with the size, and below it the audit trail of who exported what. Try: the content chips and format buttons, paint the day range, Include secrets (owner only, off by default), Build export (success), Tweaks > stage failure. Stands for: change history and the device list, which the app can already show; export formats are the app-wide requirement. Unbuilt in the app: All exports (PDF, CSV, JSON, Markdown), the preview and the audit trail are design only.

t_changes.text: Change history, write stages, takeovers, exports

s_settings.text: App settings as tiles of real controls grouped by task: a hero that searches settings through a button, quick links to the deeper boards (appearance, language, locks, tabs), people and their roles as rows with role buttons, sounds with a switch and volume, start-up behaviour and data. Try: role buttons per person, the sound switch and volume slider, start-up chips, Reset this group, Tweaks > role operator and viewer (accounts lock), lang, dark. Stands for: the owner account and the language and theme choices the app stores today. Unbuilt in the app: Roles for more people, action sounds, start-up options and settings search are design only.

s_tabs.text: How tabs work: one workspace tab per router, a row of open page tabs with a travelling indicator, and the New tab catalogue as a bento of every destination with its icon, grouped by area, with a search button beside the regex builder button and an Open every tab action. Try: the tab strip (the indicator springs across), the area chips, pin switches, tab position buttons, Open every tab, Tweaks > lang, dark, firmware stock (Merlin tabs show their lock). Stands for: the app navigation between screens. Unbuilt in the app: Tabs, the catalogue, pinning and tab layout are design only.

s_appearance.text: The look, edited live: accent as large swatches, light or dark, corner shape and density as segmented buttons, type size as a slider, a preview that uses the same components as the app, and the motion editor with a profile, a global speed and a duration, delay and distance slider per kind of motion. Try: accent swatches here mirror Tweaks > accent (change the Tweak to re-tone the whole board), the profile buttons, the per-kind switches and sliders, the speed slider; set Tweaks > motion to calm to see the editor say that reduced motion wins. Stands for: the light and dark theme choice in the app. Unbuilt in the app: Accent choice, shape, density, type size and the whole motion editor are design only.

s_language.text: Language as a live comparison: three large cards (English, Cantonese, both side by side) with the same sample screen in each, a tone slider from plain to playful with a live sample sentence, number and time formats as segmented buttons, and a drop zone for a personal wording file that stays on this computer. Try: the three language cards (they mirror Tweaks > lang: change the Tweak to translate the whole board), the tone slider, format buttons, the wording file switches, Tweaks > stage success and failure. Stands for: the English and Cantonese labels every catalogue entry already carries. Unbuilt in the app: Both-at-once mode, tone levels and the personal wording file are design only.

s_focus.text: Ways to run the app itself (not the router): Simple, Expert, Low stimulation, School and Presentation as large mode cards with what each one hides or shows, a before-and-after strip of the same screen in two modes, and switches for what a mode does. Try: pick a mode card, the detail switches per mode, the timer stepper for School mode, Tweaks > motion calm (Low stimulation implies it), role viewer. Stands for: nothing yet; the app has one layout. Unbuilt in the app: All five app modes are design only. Router bundles are the separate One-click modes board.

s_locks.text: Who can do what, as a picture: a hero with the lock state and idle timer in a ring, the three roles against every area as a paintable permission grid, per-area locks as switch tiles, signed-in sessions as rows with a sign-out button, and what always needs two keys. Try: paint the permission grid (click a cell, then another), the idle slider, area lock switches, Sign out on a session, Lock now (success), Tweaks > role operator and viewer, stage failure. Stands for: the owner account, encrypted secrets and two-key confirmation that exist today. Unbuilt in the app: App lock, operator and viewer roles, the permission grid, per-area locks and sessions are design only.

s_regex.text: A pattern you build from pieces: the pattern is a row of coloured token chips, each explained in words underneath; a library of ready patterns as segmented buttons; flags as toggle chips; and a live test against real router log lines with every match highlighted and counted. Try: the pattern buttons (tokens, explanation and highlighted matches all change, computed live), the Ignore case flag, Tweaks > lang, dark. The search bars on other boards open this builder. Stands for: plain search on the app logs screen. Unbuilt in the app: The builder is design only and is far from full parity with a dedicated regex tool: no token editing by hand, no replace, no flavours other than JavaScript, no debugger, no library saving.

s_updates.text: App updates you can see coming: a hero for a build that is being made right now (Update coming soon) with its number, a pipeline of build stages each with its own state, start time and elapsed time, a labelled estimate, what the build will contain, and when it becomes an ordinary offer. Try: Tweaks > stage (loading, empty = up to date, success = updated, failure = checksum), the channel buttons, the install-when buttons, role viewer. Stands for: the app version shown in settings. Unbuilt in the app: Self-update, Update coming soon with live build stages and update history are design only.

t_app.text: Settings, tabs, appearance, language, modes, locks, regex, updates

s_toolbox.text: Network helpers that need no router: a subnet calculator driven by a prefix stepper with a network-and-host bar and counts, a QR maker, a MAC vendor lookup with a device picker, a port reference as chips, a unit converter with sliders and a signal-strength guide as a gauge. Try: the prefix stepper (bar and counts follow), the last-octet stepper, the port preset chips, the converter slider, the signal slider, Tweaks > lang, dark. Stands for: nothing yet; these are app-side tools that do not talk to the router. Unbuilt in the app: The whole toolbox is design only.

s_servermanager.text: A Minecraft server creator and manager that sits naturally in a router app, because a server needs a reserved address and a port forward: server cards with players and memory gauges, a create flow as pickers (edition, version, flavour, target), the four run targets as large cards, a live console and the router wiring it needs. Try: the edition and flavour buttons, version stepper, target cards, memory slider, Start (success), Tweaks > stage failure (out of memory), role operator. Stands for: nothing yet. The router side (reserve an address, forward a port) already exists in the write path. Unbuilt in the app: The whole server manager is design only: version discovery, plugin install and the four targets (local process, local Docker, SSH process, SSH Docker).

s_deploy.text: One-click deployment of the web app form of this app: five targets as large cards (Docker, VirtualBox, VMware, USB stick for a spare PC, Raspberry Pi card), a deployment pipeline with live progress, the instance manager with health and actions per instance, and the working link as a QR after each deploy. Try: pick a target card, the port presets, Deploy (success with the link), Tweaks > stage failure (port clash), instance switches and actions, role operator (flashing a disk is owner only). Stands for: the app already runs as a self-hosted web app and as a Windows desktop app. Unbuilt in the app: The deploy assistant, appliance images, virtual machine import, disk flashing and the instance manager are design only.

s_docs.text: The public documentation website: a hero that leads with tasks instead of a file list, task cards with icons and reading time, an interactive "what happens when you apply a change" walkthrough with step buttons, an article reader preview with contents, and the delivery forms (website, offline app, phone PDF). Try: the walkthrough step buttons (the pipeline and the explanation move), the task filter chips, the reading-size slider, the edition buttons, Tweaks > lang, dark. Stands for: the documentation website published with the project (99 articles, a wiki and a phone PDF edition). Unbuilt in the app: This board is the design the website should move toward; screenshots in it are placeholders until captures of a built release exist.

s_help.text: Help inside the app: a hero offering a guided tour of the current page, tours as cards with progress rings that remember where you stopped, keyboard shortcuts as key caps, the offline documentation with its freshness, and a what-changed strip for the installed version. Try: Start a tour, the tour progress cards, the shortcut scheme buttons, Read aloud switch, Tweaks > lang, dark, motion calm. Stands for: the help text every catalogue entry carries (shown beside each control). Unbuilt in the app: Guided tours, shortcuts sheet and bundled offline docs are design only.

s_sshactions.text: Every action the app can run on the router over SSH, as cards sorted into four lanes by how much confirmation each one needs: runs at once, preview first, preview and guard, four keys. A filter by kind, the exact command on every card, and a sheet that states what the command does, how it is confirmed, the brother level it carries and whether it can be undone. Try: the kind filter chips (lanes refill), click any card (the sheet rises with the exact command), Run it (a toast confirms), open Restart the router (it sends you to the four keys instead of running), Tweaks > role viewer and operator, stage failure, lang. Stands for: the SSH command runner and the write path that already exist; the app already runs nvram, service and log commands. Unbuilt in the app: The catalogue as one browsable list, the four lanes, the per-action sheet and the brother level per action are design only.

s_terminal.text: A real shell on the router, for the owner role only: a large terminal with the session so far, one-tap commands that type and run themselves, a stop that catches dangerous commands and hands them to the four keys, session recording, an idle lock and a paste guard. Operators and viewers see a locked card with the reason. Try: the one-tap commands (output is appended with a live cursor), Try to reboot (the app stops it), Clear, the recording switch, the idle slider, Tweaks > role operator (the terminal locks), firmware, lang. Stands for: the SSH connection the app already holds; today it only runs catalogue commands. Unbuilt in the app: The free terminal, the dangerous-command stop, recording, the idle lock and the paste guard are design only.

s_entware.text: Extra software for Asuswrt-Merlin, kept on a USB drive: Entware health and space, a package shelf with install toggles, the well-known Merlin add-ons as cards with switches, updates waiting, the custom-script switches and the live package log. On stock firmware every tile shows locked with the reason. Try: the package chips (each queues an install into pending changes), the add-on switches, Update all (success), Tweaks > firmware stock (tiles lock with the reason), stage empty and failure, lang. Stands for: nothing yet. The router side is plain SSH: opkg and the add-on installer scripts. Unbuilt in the app: The whole area is design only: Entware setup, the package shelf, add-on cards and script switches.

s_flashbackup.text: A byte-for-byte copy of the router flash, read over SSH and never written: the flash as a proportional strip of its six parts, each part as a timeline row with its size, what it holds and its checksum once verified, the copy rate, where the copy is kept and what it is for. Try: Copy the next part (the strip fills, the row turns green and its checksum appears), Start again, Tweaks > stage success and failure, role viewer, lang. Stands for: the SSH connection; the app already reads files from the router. Unbuilt in the app: Reading the flash parts, the double-read check and the kept-copies list are design only.

t_ssh.text: SSH action catalogue, owner terminal, Entware, flash backup

s_firmwareupload.text: Uploading a firmware file by hand, as five steps you can see: choose the file (a drop zone that is also a button), five checks that all must pass, the four keys, then the dim sum moment: while the router writes the image and restarts there is nothing useful to press, so the screen says so with a bamboo steamer, rising steam and five buns that fill in as the stages finish. Then the router is back. Try: Start over, Choose the file, Run the five checks, Write it (the dim sum moment appears), The router is back; Try a file for another model (it opens the screen that shows three words); Tweaks > motion calm (steam stops, buns rest in place), stage success and failure, role viewer, lang. Stands for: the firmware domain: installed version and check-for-update. Unbuilt in the app: Manual upload, the five checks, the dim sum moment and the back-online check are design only.

s_dimsumonly.text: The refusal screen. When a firmware file is for another model, or its signature has been changed, the whole app is replaced by one screen that says "Hong Kong Dim Sum" and nothing else: no reason, no alternative, no button. Under it (click anywhere, or change the stage Tweak) is the ordinary record of what was refused and proof that the router was not touched. Try: click anywhere on the screen (it lifts and the record underneath shows), Show the screen again, Tweaks > stage (loading, empty, success and failure show the record page), motion calm (the steam stops), dark, accent, lang (the three words do not change). Stands for: nothing yet. Unbuilt in the app: The whole refusal screen and the refusal record are design only.

t_fwup.text: Firmware upload, the dim sum moment and the three-word screen

s_livemode.text: Live mode: an app-wide switch that writes each small change the moment you make it instead of collecting it for Apply. A hero with the big Live switch, six everyday switches to try it on, the undo toast with its eight-second bar, what is never live (anything that can cut the connection, anything with keys), a live feed and how long Live mode stays on. Try: flip any of the six switches (a toast slides in with Undo and a draining bar; the row gets a live mark), Undo on the toast, Keep, turn Live mode off and flip again (the change waits in the pending dock instead), Tweaks > role viewer, motion calm, lang. Stands for: the write path: today every change is previewed and applied on request. Unbuilt in the app: Live mode, the undo toast and the never-live list are design only.

s_historymanager.text: Everything the router has ever been told, as something you can work with: a timeline you can select from, a before-and-after diff of one change or of everything between two points, the life of one setting across months, restore to any point, statistics (who, what, when, how often undone) and a simulation panel that shows what a restore would do to the house before you run it. Try: click a timeline entry (the diff follows), Compare with... then a second entry (the diff becomes everything between them), Clear, Restore to just before this (a banner confirms), the per-setting buttons (the value trail changes), Now and After restore in the simulation panel, Tweaks > role viewer, stage failure, lang. Stands for: the app change history with undo for single entries. Unbuilt in the app: Compare between two points, per-setting history, restore to a point, statistics and the simulation panel are design only.

t_live.text: Live mode and the History manager

s_fourkey.text: The confirmation for actions that cannot be undone (restart, firmware, factory reset): four keys in a row, each a different real control so that no single slip or habit gets through. Key 1 is a switch saying you know what will happen, key 2 is picking this router out of three, key 3 is setting a dial to the number shown, key 4 only turns after the other three. An arming bar fills as they turn, and the launch pad opens only when all four are on. Try: turn key 1 off and on, pick a wrong router (key 2 goes back and says so), step the dial to 7 (key 3 turns), then Turn the last key (the bar fills and the launch pad opens), Pull all keys; Tweaks > role operator (owner only: the keys lock), stage success and failure, motion calm, lang. Stands for: the two-key confirmation for destructive actions that the app already has. Unbuilt in the app: Four keys, the three different key controls, the arming bar and the expiry are design only.

s_brothermad.text: The full-screen Level 3 warning, "Prepare for brother mad", which takes over the whole app when an action would cut someone off for minutes in the middle of something that matters: hazard stripes, an angry face that shakes and steams, exactly what he is doing and what he will lose, and three ways on (wait until he is done, warn him first, or accept it and go to the four keys). Under it: the four levels as cards and what decides the level. Try: Wait until he is done (the warning lifts), Show the Level 3 warning again, the four level cards (the meter and the wording follow; only Level 3 has the takeover), I accept (goes to the four keys), Tweaks > motion standard and calm (stripes, shaking and steam stop), dark, accent, lang, stage. Stands for: nothing yet. The app knows which devices are online; it does not yet know what they are doing. Unbuilt in the app: Levels, activity detection and the full-screen warning are design only.

s_missilelaunch.text: Restarting the router, staged as a launch so that it is impossible to do absent-mindedly: a night-sky launch pad with the rocket on it, a go or hold checklist, a ten-second count with Abort in reach the whole time, lift-off when the command is really sent, and then a hand-over to the live reboot timeline. Below: the sequence, what is actually sent, abort rules and how to switch the show off. Try: Abort (the pad says nothing was sent), Reset, Start the count (flames and smoke start, the count runs), Launch now (lift-off: the rocket climbs, the tower falls away, the scene shakes), Watch the reboot live; Tweaks > motion calm (a still pad with a plain 10), role operator (owner only), stage success and failure, lang. Stands for: the reboot command behind the two-key confirmation. Unbuilt in the app: The launch pad, the checklist, the count with abort and the hand-over to the timeline are design only.

s_reboottimeline.text: What happens after lift-off, live: a hero with the elapsed time and a seven-point timeline whose marker travels as each stage is seen (command sent, SSH closed, radios down, system starting, internet up, Wi-Fi up, devices back), a ping strip that turns red while the router is silent, each stage with its expected and actual time, the devices rejoining one by one, how the brother level cools as things return, and what the app does if the router does not come back. Try: Next stage (the marker travels, the ping strip grows, devices turn green, the level cools), Replay from the start, Tweaks > stage success and failure (not back after 5 minutes), motion calm, role viewer (can watch), lang. Stands for: nothing yet: today the app simply loses its connection during a restart. Unbuilt in the app: Listening for the router during a restart, the timeline, the ping strip and the rejoin list are design only.

t_danger.text: Four keys, the Level 3 warning, the reboot launch and its live timeline

s_household.text: The people behind the devices. A hero card for "Your brother" with his presence chip and what he is doing right now, a tile for his name, devices and notices, "Most brother madness allowed" as a four-step control with a meter and a plain sentence for each step, protected hours painted on a week grid, the Home Assistant connection with entity pickers, the presence chip in its four states and everyone else in the house. Try: the four presence states (the chip, the sentence and the level meter follow), Most brother madness allowed 0 to 3 (the sentence changes and the change queues), paint protected hours (click one cell then another), the presets, the device chips, the Home Assistant entity picker and switches, Tweaks > role viewer, stage failure, lang. Stands for: the device list with names. Unbuilt in the app: People, the brother card, the allowed level, protected hours, the Home Assistant link and the presence chip are design only.

s_leaderboard.text: A leaderboard of who is using the connection, with two tabs. "Who's using the most" ranks devices by download plus upload on a podium and a bar list. "Who's uploading or downloading the most" splits the two directions: a Downloading or Uploading switch re-ranks the podium, and two lists sit side by side, because the device that uploads the most (a camera, a backup) is rarely the one that downloads the most. Period buttons cover right now, today, 7 days and 30 days, and any row can be slowed down. Try: the two tabs (the indicator springs across and the page changes), Downloading and Uploading on the second tab (the podium and the headline change), the period buttons (Right now switches to Mbps and reorders), Slow down on a row (it queues a limit into pending changes), Tweaks > role viewer, stage failure, lang. Stands for: the device list; the router already keeps per-device traffic counters when statistics are on. Unbuilt in the app: The ranking, both tabs, the periods and the one-tap limit are design only.

t_household.text: Household and who is using the most

s_wifidiag.text: Why the Wi-Fi is slow, worked out for you: a health score with a radar of nearby networks, findings in order of how much they hurt with a one-tap fix on each, one device under the microscope (signal over the last hour with its roams), who is using the air on each band, retries by device, roaming and drop events as a timeline, a walk test that paints signal as you move, and how the test itself is run. Try: the device picker (one device at a time), the band buttons, the fix buttons (success), the walk-test switch, the probe slider, Tweaks > stage failure (radio off), role viewer, motion calm (the radar stills), lang. Stands for: the wireless domain: clients, signal and channel per band are already read. Unbuilt in the app: The health score, findings with fixes, per-device history, airtime split, the roaming timeline and the walk test are design only.

s_portshardware.text: The box itself: the back panel drawn as real sockets you can click, with link lights and speeds; the selected port with its speed, what is plugged in and its settings; temperatures as gauges, the processor and memory over the last hour, the lights with a night schedule, what the buttons on the case do, the USB ports and power draw. Try: click each socket on the back panel (the port card follows; LAN 3 shows the slow link, LAN 4 shows empty), the speed buttons, the lights switch and brightness, the WPS button role, Tweaks > firmware stock (the lights tile locks), stage failure, role viewer, lang. Stands for: the system domain: model, uptime, load and memory. Unbuilt in the app: The back panel, per-port speeds and settings, temperatures, lights, button roles and power draw are design only.

s_services.text: Everything the router itself runs and who can reach it: each service as a card with a switch and its port, the question "who can open the router page" answered with three large choices, the certificate with its days left as a gauge, sign-in protection, the addresses allowed in from outside, and an outside check that lists what the internet can actually see. Try: the service switches (each queues a change), the three web access choices, the port pickers with presets, the lock-out stepper, the allowed address picker, Check from outside (success), Tweaks > stage failure, role viewer, lang. Stands for: the settings catalogue already covers SSH, web access and UPnP as plain fields. Unbuilt in the app: The service cards, the outside check, the certificate gauge and sign-in protection are design only.

s_cloud.text: Every way the router talks to somebody else's servers, in one place: a live map of the links that are on, each cloud feature as a card with a switch and a plain sentence about what it sends, a tile that lists what leaves the house and what never does, the linked account, and one switch that cuts all of them at once. Try: the feature switches, Cut every cloud link (success), the data-sharing switches, Unlink the account (failure), Tweaks > firmware stock (the names change), role viewer, motion calm (packets stop), lang. Stands for: nothing yet. Unbuilt in the app: The whole cloud page is design only: the link map, feature cards, the data list and the cut-all switch.

t_services.text: Network services, web access and cloud

s_firewallinternals.text: What the firewall actually does, under the friendly rules: the path a packet takes through the five chains as boxes you can click, the real rules of the selected chain with how many packets each one has matched, the connection table as a gauge with its busiest devices, a packet tracer that shows which rule would decide a given connection, the dropped-packet log and, on Asuswrt-Merlin, custom rules. Try: click each chain on the packet path (the rule list and its description change), the table buttons, the tracer device and port pickers, Trace (success), Tweaks > firmware stock (custom rules lock), role viewer, stage failure, lang. Stands for: the firewall domain as on or off settings and port forwards. Unbuilt in the app: Reading chains and counters, the connection table, the tracer and custom rules are design only.

s_guestpro.text: Guest networks done properly: the five Guest Pro profiles as cards with switches (party, shop, kids, smart home, VPN), a designer for the page guests see before they get online with a live phone preview that follows every choice, three ways in (one tap, a passcode, printed vouchers), time and speed limits, vouchers with a QR code, and the guests online now with a way to end a visit. Try: the portal style buttons (the phone preview changes title and colour), the three ways in (the preview button and field change), the terms switch, the limit sliders, Make vouchers, Publish (success), End visit on a guest, Tweaks > stage failure, role viewer, lang. Stands for: the guest Wi-Fi on or off setting per band. Unbuilt in the app: Profiles, the captive portal and its designer, vouchers, limits and the live guest list are design only.

s_dsl.text: The phone-line side of a DSL router (the example is a DSL-AX82U; the RT-AX86U used elsewhere on the canvas has no DSL port, and its empty stage says so): sync speeds and margin as a hero, the tones that carry the data drawn one bar each with download and upload bands and a notch, margin over a day, error counters, the stability slider and line switches, what a resync costs, and line events as a timeline. Try: the stability slider, the mode buttons, the line switches, Resync the line (success; the hero warns it costs a minute and asks at brother Level 2), Tweaks > stage empty (no DSL port on this model) and failure, role viewer, motion calm, lang. Stands for: nothing yet: the app has only been used with Ethernet-WAN models. Unbuilt in the app: The whole DSL page is design only.

s_routeraddon.text: The page the add-on adds to the router's own web interface, drawn in the style of the Asuswrt-Merlin administration pages (the dark grey #4D595D panel) and not in the app's style, because that is where it lives. Title "Material Router", On and Off, the port (8790), "Which version opens (remembered by this browser)" with a Material version card and an Advanced version card, the Open link, and the note that switching it on or off restarts only this app. Try: On and Off (the Open link leaves when it is off); the port buttons (the link follows); the two version cards (the link text and address follow); Apply; Tweaks > lang, accent (only the Open link takes the accent), role viewer. Dark has no effect here on purpose: the router page has one look. Stands for: the add-on page on the router (addon/webui), reached from the router's own menu. Unbuilt in the app: Nothing on this board is missing from the add-on.

s_phone.text: Phone home: the same dashboard folded to one column. A hero with the live rate and a traffic line, two half-width number tiles, quick switches as large rows, and the bottom navigation with a sliding pill. Try: the quick switches, Tweaks > stage (loading skeleton, empty, failure), lang, dark, role viewer. Stands for: the overview screen at phone width. Unbuilt in the app: Live rate, quick switches and the bottom navigation are design only.

s_phonewifi.text: Phone Wi-Fi: the band tiles become a swipe-free stack, each with its radio switch and a gauge; width and power are thumb-size controls; pending changes collect in a bottom sheet that rises over the page with Preview and Apply. Try: flip a radio or change the width: the bottom sheet rises with the count; Discard; Tweaks > stage success and failure, role viewer. Stands for: the Wi-Fi band settings at phone width. Unbuilt in the app: The bottom sheet and gauges are design only.

s_phonenav.text: Where every desktop destination lands on a phone: a search button with the regex button beside it, area chips, and all areas as a two-column grid of shaped icon tiles, so nothing from the desktop rail is lost. Try: the area chips, Tweaks > firmware stock (VPN Director shows its lock), lang, dark, stage empty. Stands for: the app navigation list. Unbuilt in the app: Search, pinning and the grid are design only.

s_phonedevices.text: Phone devices: device rows with icon tiles and status chips, and the device sheet that rises from the bottom with the same actions as the desktop panel (block, reserve, priority) as thumb-size controls. Try: the sheet switch in the app bar area (Device sheet), block and reserve switches, priority buttons, Tweaks > role viewer, stage. Stands for: the devices screen at phone width. Unbuilt in the app: The device sheet is design only.

s_phoneguard.text: The guard takeover on a phone: the whole screen is the question. A real countdown inside a rotating wavy ring, one full-width confirm action in the thumb zone, a quieter roll-back action and what will be restored. Try: I am still connected (success), Roll back now (failure), Tweaks > stage, motion calm (the ring stills, the number stays), lang. Stands for: the connection-loss guard, at phone width. Unbuilt in the app: The wavy ring; the guard logic exists.

s_phonetools.text: Phone tools: the tool picker as a segmented control, a result hero with the average and a latency line, target chips, and the live log as a short terminal. Try: the tool buttons, target chips, Run (success), Tweaks > stage failure. Stands for: ping, traceroute and lookup run on the router. Unbuilt in the app: The latency line and live log are design only.

s_phonesetup.text: First run on a phone: a radar finds the router, the five steps are a compact pipeline, the sign-in method is two thumb-size buttons, and the single Next action sits in the thumb zone. Try: the sign-in buttons, the reveal eye, Next (success), Tweaks > stage loading, empty and failure. Stands for: the first-run screens at phone width. Unbuilt in the app: The scan radar is design only.

s_phonesettings.text: Phone settings: the four notifications that need you as a stack, then look, language and motion as thumb-size segmented controls, and the app lock switch. Try: the language, theme and motion buttons (they mirror the Tweaks), the lock switch, Tweaks > lang, dark, motion. Stands for: the language and theme choices the app stores. Unbuilt in the app: The notification stack and motion choice are design only.

t_phone.text: Phone boards: where every desktop feature lands

s_rail.text: The frosted navigation rail every desktop board imports: brand mark in a cookie shape, the Review changes action with its pending count, and every area grouped as Network, Visual editors, Router and App. Try: Tweaks > page (any id such as wifi, edmap, history) to move the active pill, pending (0 hides the badge and stops the rotating border), firmware stock (VPN Director shows Merlin only), lang, dark, accent, motion. Stands for: the app navigation list in the left column. Unbuilt in the app: The Visual editors group and One-click modes entries do not exist in the app yet.

s_topbar.text: The top bar every desktop board imports: a large condensed page title, the search-everything button (a button that opens the palette, not a text box), firmware chip, language, notifications with an unread badge, the signed-in person, and the page tabs. Try: click the tabs (the indicator springs across), Tweaks > title, tabs (comma separated), active, role, firmware, lang, dark. Stands for: the app header. Unbuilt in the app: The search palette and per-page tabs are design only.
